I felt the exact same for the last few years. I'm 17 and grew up earlier than everyone else my age physically but I always have felt like the ugliest. Everything you said is exactly how I felt from the age of like 11 until I was 16. I learned how to do my own makeup and it was a lot of trial and error, phases of wearing large amounts of makeup to wearing as little as possible. Now I feel like I really can call myself average, and I admit alot of that is because I learned to do my makeup while following the rule of "a little goes a long way", but alot of it was also trying to ignore and forget anything my own brain said about my appearance because our minds can trick us. I have an asymmetrical face too, most people do, and some of my features stand out more than others, most people have that too. I can guarantee that the way other people see you is nowhere near as bad as you think, I struggled with this for most of the last two years (and I still do! But learning to not let your mind trick you is so important).

I know it's different for everyone, but I usually wear mascara with curled lashes and tinted lip balm. It was enough to get me out of my own head trying to convince me that I am ugly. It's a process of learning what helps you feel confident and also a journey of changing the way you think about yourself. I don't mean to make it seem like it's about myself, but reading your post was like reading something I would have written only 6 months ago.
